I’m 57 years old and I’ve been working these fields in Quzhou for more than three decades. I finished senior high school, so I read the extension bulletins and I pay attention to what the agricultural college says, but I also trust what I’ve seen with my own eyes on my own land. I’ve got 12 mu in total. The core of my farm is the wheat–maize double crop on 9 mu—that’s the system that pays the bills. The winter wheat went in last October and right now it’s at jointing stage, so my immediate work is the spring topdressing and irrigation. I’m keeping 3 mu in cotton this year because the price has been steady and it spreads my risk if the maize market dips.

For the wheat, I’m targeting about 950 kg/mu. I’ll put down roughly 38 kg of nitrogen per mu: 100 kg of compound fertilizer as a base dressing, then about 40 kg of urea at topdressing now in April. I know that’s above the extension recommendation, but I got over 900 kg/mu last year doing exactly this, and I’d rather waste a little fertilizer than lose a big chunk of yield. I’m also applying about 15 kg each of phosphorus and potassium per mu through the compound fertilizer to keep the balance. I’ll irrigate four times total for the wheat—including the winter irrigation I already did and the two spring irrigations plus one more at filling.

The summer maize will go in directly after wheat harvest in early June. There is no time for ploughing; I’ll use no-tillage direct seeding with hybrid Denghai 605, which is what my most successful neighbor uses. I’ll give it about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu from one bag of compound fertilizer, plus 6 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. Two irrigations should be enough for maize if the summer rains are normal, and I’ll spray herbicide and insecticide three times total.

For cotton, I rotary-tilled the 3 mu last week and I’m planting improved Guoxinmian now. Cotton is labor-intensive—it’ll need about 12 pesticide applications through the season for bollworm and aphids—but the returns are good. I’ll apply around 21 kg of nitrogen per mu, split between a base compound dressing and a urea topdressing, with about 12 kg each of phosphorus and potassium, and irrigate twice.

I watch the pumping costs closely because our tube wells are metered now, so I’m not going beyond what I’ve just described. That’s my plan for the year.
